sections.title: arXiv Biology and Biomedicine — 2026-11-24 announcement batch
sections.text: Ten notable recent papers; relevance-oriented ordering because no candidates had detected HF or HN attention. arXiv has no official trending chart and incomplete biomedical coverage.
sections.global_caveat: ArXiv is not a representative index of biomedical research; much clinical and experimental work appears on bioRxiv or medRxiv.

sections.title: General-purpose language models are neurosymbolic reasoners able to annotate proteins from sequence
sections.abstract: The authors tested general-purpose language models on protein-annotation tasks, including Pfam domains, catalytic-residue loss, and structure or activity prediction, reporting above-chance performance.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint argues that generalist models can combine sequence and symbolic reasoning for protein annotation; its tests were above chance, and the authors report confident hallucinations as well as correct calls.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors did not benchmark against specialized tools, and the paper reports model predictions rather than experimental validation of protein function.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 0.50, entirely from 2 cross-lists; no HF upvotes or HN points/comments were recorded.

sections.title: VEGA: A Scalable Software-Hardware Co-design for Genome Alignment using RVV Extension
sections.abstract: VEGA combines RISC-V vector instructions and a software-hardware design to accelerate dynamic-programming genome alignment, reporting up to 15.1× and 9.7× speedups for Edit Distance and Smith–Waterman versus the Ara2-RVV vector baseline.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint reports algorithm benchmarks and post-synthesis hardware results, including 1.0% area overhead against a standard RISC-V core.
sections.unique_caveat: These are computational and synthesis evaluations, not biological validation; the reported speedups are relative to the stated vector baseline.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 0.50, entirely from 2 cross-lists; no HF upvotes or HN points/comments were recorded.

sections.title: Nonequilibrium fluctuations could explain the hot mitochondria paradox
sections.abstract: The authors propose that nonequilibrium cellular fluctuations and frequency-sensitive molecular thermometers could produce apparent mitochondrial temperature elevations without a true steady-state 10 K gradient.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint offers a physical explanation for previously reported apparent mitochondrial temperature differences, arguing that probe response to nonequilibrium fluctuations could account for them at biologically attainable power.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a theoretical proposal, not a new measurement or experimental test of the proposed probe mechanism.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 0.50, entirely from 2 cross-lists; no HF upvotes or HN points/comments were recorded.

sections.title: FastCREST: GPU-Accelerated CREST Conformer Searches with Consistent Energies and Gradients
sections.abstract: FastCREST distributes and GPU-accelerates CREST molecular conformer searches, reporting faster evaluations and close agreement with CREST 3.0.2 for energies, gradients, and tested conformer searches.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint reports a complete 274-atom gallium(III)-peptide search taking 54.3 hours versus 321.5 hours for the stated CREST 3.0.2 run, with hardware differences noted by the authors.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is computational benchmarking on a limited set of molecules; speed and numerical agreement do not establish improved agreement with experimental conformations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 0.00, with 0 cross-lists and no detected HF or HN engagement; zero is not evidence of unimportance.

sections.title: Towards Edge Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Antimicrobial Resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
sections.abstract: The authors combine 4-mer whole-genome features and a Random Forest to predict resistance across 20 antibiotics, reporting mean ROC AUC 0.82 on an independent test set.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint presents a lightweight genomic prediction pipeline intended for resource-constrained devices and reports the independent-test AUC above.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not give cohort size or external-site composition; this is a model evaluation, not prospective clinical validation or evidence of improved treatment outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 0.25, entirely from 1 cross-list; no HF upvotes or HN points/comments were recorded.

sections.title: A scalar arterial input function does not uniquely determine the perfusion residue: Theory and phantom MRI
sections.abstract: A flow model and 3 T straight-tube phantom experiment show that the same cross-sectionally averaged arterial input function can correspond to different tracer curves and perfusion residues.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint derives the residue under stated flow assumptions and reports phantom enhancement differences at all 11 measurement stations across three boluses, with model-dependent tissue curves differing by up to 23.3% of the uniform-inlet peak.
sections.unique_caveat: The validation is a straight-tube phantom plus an idealized model, not a patient study; the authors challenge interpretation of the scalar-input model rather than demonstrate a clinical effect.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 0.25, entirely from 1 cross-list; no HF upvotes or HN points/comments were recorded.

sections.title: MRI-Driven Dual-Energy CT Synthesis via Conditional Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models for MRI-only Radiotherapy and Protontherapy
sections.abstract: A conditional diffusion model synthesizes high- and low-energy CT images from MRI and, in retrospective paired head-and-neck proton-therapy data, outperformed two GAN baselines on reported image-quality measures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint reports mean absolute errors of 36.29±5.25 HU and 43.72±6.77 HU for the synthesized high- and low-energy CT, respectively, and compares against Pix2PixGAN and CycleGAN.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not state cohort size and describes retrospective image validation, not prospective workflow or patient-outcome testing.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 0.25, entirely from 1 cross-list; no HF upvotes or HN points/comments were recorded.

sections.title: High-Resolution 3D Micro-CT Database of Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) Coils for More Accurate Modelling, Technology Benchmarking, and Progress in Coil Design
sections.abstract: The authors use high-resolution micro-CT and electrical measurements to create a modelling dataset for 17 commercial TMS coils and demonstrate a CT-derived coil model in simulation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint provides coil geometry and impedance data, with micro-CT at 0.0495 mm resolution and a simulation example reporting differences from an existing SimNIBS coil model.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a hardware characterization and simulation resource; it does not test TMS effectiveness or safety outcomes in people.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 0.25, entirely from 1 cross-list; no HF upvotes or HN points/comments were recorded.

sections.title: Multi-Sensor Fusion for False-Alarm Reduction by Timed Electromechanical Corroboration
sections.abstract: In ECG recordings with injected beat-shaped artifacts, the authors report that adding mechanically sensed contraction timing reduced artifact acceptance while retaining most true beats.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint reports 6.2% of injected artifacts passing and 95% of true beats retained with a selected two-sensor setup, and says integer microcontroller decisions matched software.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly state that natural motion and clinical events remain untested; injected-artifact performance is not evidence of patient-monitor alarm performance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 0.25, entirely from 1 cross-list; no HF upvotes or HN points/comments were recorded.

sections.title: Linking vascular pathways to organ anatomical structures in the Human Reference Atlas
sections.abstract: The authors add machine-readable crosswalks linking blood and lymphatic vascular pathways with anatomy, cataloguing 349 vessels and 663 links to 295 structures across 20 organs or body regions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint reports algorithmic checks and review by 11 organ experts for the crosswalk tables and diagrams.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an anatomical knowledge and data-modeling contribution; it documents and organizes existing knowledge rather than experimentally validating vascular function.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 0.00, with 0 cross-lists and no detected HF or HN engagement; zero is not evidence of unimportance.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.text: Computational methods span protein annotation, molecular conformer search, genome alignment, and tuberculosis resistance prediction (papers 1, 2, 4, 5); imaging papers examine measurement assumptions and model fidelity (6–8); dataset and sensor-fusion work provides biomedical infrastructure without outcome evidence (9–10); paper 3 proposes a theoretical explanation for apparent mitochondrial heating.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.text: Follow-up needs include benchmarking protein-language-model annotations against specialized pipelines and blinded assays (1); external, geographically separate MTB resistance validation and calibration (5); more realistic vascular tests and external/prospective imaging evaluation (6–8); and direct experiments varying mitochondrial probe frequency response to test the proposed nonequilibrium mechanism (3). These are research proposals, not clinical recommendations.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The batch has relevant technical contributions but no detected popularity signals and no Semantic Scholar citation corroboration. Its evidence ranges from computation and theory to phantom and retrospective data; none should be read as established clinical findings.
